findings.mechanism: Each parsed Tree forms reference cycles (Node.parent <-> parent.children, Node.tree <-> Tree.root/by_path), so refcounting alone never frees them; only the cyclic GC does. outlines/tuning.py:11 raises the gen0 threshold to 40,000, so garbage trees pile up for a while between collections and the memory graph climbs.
findings.cause: gc.set_threshold(40000, 20, 20) in tuning.install(), called from every OutlineService() constructor, delays cyclic collection; nothing holds the trees after convert() returns (OutlineService keeps only an int counter, OutlineResult holds only strings/ints).
findings.evidence: Ran 30000 conversions through OutlineService: gc.get_objects() count sawtooths (24k, 34k, 47k, then 15k, 26k, 38k, 47k, 18k ...) with gen2 collections still firing; RSS flat at 22 MB; after gc.collect() live objects fall to ~11.7k; switching to the default threshold and running 30000 more left RSS at 22 MB and ~13k objects.
findings.discriminator: Object count and RSS are bounded and drop back to baseline whenever the cyclic GC runs (gc.collect() reclaims everything); no long-lived container, global, cache or registration table references the trees. It is a deferred-collection sawtooth, not unbounded retention. Mitigation: lower or remove the threshold override, or break cycles (weakref parent/tree).
